subject: Coverage windows & price protection for reserved capacity
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Carter <emily@pulseai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Coverage windows & price protection for reserved capacity

Hi Emily — great meeting this morning.

Thanks again for walking us through PulseAI's inference growth playbook. Per our convo the two asks we hear most from procurement are: (1) a commitment term that doesn't lock customers into long tail exposure if GPU pricing drops, and (2) predictable unit economics for budgeting.

I attached an initial one-pager called "coverage_windows_v1.pdf" that sketches a possible structure we discussed:
- Coverage window: a 12-month reserved capacity term split into a core committed baseline (e.g., 70% of booked QPS) + a burst buffer that can be scheduled on demand.
- Pricing floor/corridor: if wholesale GPU costs move materially (down or up) beyond a predefined corridor, we trigger either a credit or an escalation review.
- Escalation path: automatic credits up to a threshold; larger adjustments require finance approval.

High level: this gives PulseAI budget certainty while sharing some market risk with Redwood vs. a full fixed-price lock. We can also offer a short pilot (3 months) that converts into the 12-month coverage with a retroactive credit if list prices fall.

Next steps: please confirm which of the three options (core+burst, fixed tier, or pilot-first) you'd prefer. Happy to pull in finance for any deeper discount asks.

Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Attachment: coverage_windows_v1.pdf (PDF, 1 page)

From: Emily Carter <emily@pulseai.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@pulseai.com
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Coverage windows & price protection for reserved capacity

Hi Rafael — thanks for the clear summary and the one-pager. Procurement here liked the hybrid idea; a couple of follow-ups from their side:

1) Price volatility: they want stronger downside protection if GPU spot/list prices drop > 15% in any quarter — essentially a rebate rather than a future credit.
2) Tenor: PulseAI prefers not to commit to 12 months for a first enterprise deployment; they asked if we can start with 6 months and then ladder to 12 if latency/throughput KPIs hit targets.
3) Auditability: they need usage & audit logs and a monthly cost reconciliation CSV.

Also tagging procurement (procurement@pulseai.com) to coordinate legal. Can you confirm whether rebates would require exec approval? If so, please loop in finance.

Emily Carter
Head of Cloud Ops | PulseAI Systems

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Carter <emily@pulseai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, procurement@pulseai.com
Date: Mon, 18 Aug 2025 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Coverage windows & price protection for reserved capacity

Emily — really helpful questions. Quick answers and a proposed path forward below.

On 2025-08-15 Emily Carter wrote:
> 1) Price volatility: they want stronger downside protection if GPU spot/list prices drop > 15% in any quarter — essentially a rebate rather than a future credit.

We can do a rebate-style protection but it drives margin exposure. Proposed structure (attached matrix pricing_floor_matrix.xlsx):
- Safety corridor +/-12% by quarter: automatic rolling credit applied to next invoice up to 5% of quarterly committed spend.
- Deep drop (>12%): rebate applied at quarter close up to 12% of committed spend, subject to finance cap and a 6-month lookback.

> 2) Tenor: PulseAI prefers not to commit to 12 months for a first enterprise deployment; they asked if we can start with 6 months and then ladder to 12 if KPIs hit targets.

We can offer a 6->12 ladder: initial 6 months with fixed per-token pricing and the coverage window model kicking in on conversion. If they convert to 12 months within the first 6-month window, we can apply a one-time conversion credit (to compensate for the difference if list prices have fallen).

> 3) Auditability: they need usage & audit logs and a monthly cost reconciliation CSV.

Redwood can provide token-level billing + per-route latency/cost CSVs (we already expose this in the Console). I'll include a link to the sample monthly reconciliation export.

Approvals: any rebate >8% of committed spend needs finance exec sign-off. Ben — can you confirm if we can approve up to 12% under a capped program for strategic pilots and what the required review cycles would be?

Proposed next step: if PulseAI is comfortable with the ladder + corridor, I'll draft term language and a mutual action plan (MAP).

— Rafael

Attachment: pricing_floor_matrix.xlsx (Excel, 2 sheets)
Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/PLS-2025-0893

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Emily Carter <emily@pulseai.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Aug 2025 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Coverage windows & price protection for reserved capacity

Thanks Rafael — reviewed. Internal note for the thread:

- Finance is okay to support a pilot program with a rebate corridor as described, with the following guardrails:
  * Auto-credit up to 5% quarterly (operationally innocuous).
  * Rebate up to 12% at quarter close requires a brief finance review (48-hour SLA) and a signed amendment.
  * Maximum cumulative rebate exposure per customer in a 12-month rolling period capped at 18% of committed spend.

Ben (cc'd) confirms we can fast-track sign-off for strategic logos; anything beyond the 12% rebate or outside the cap will require CFO approval.

Emily — if that sounds acceptable, Rafael and I will publish a short MAP and term addendum that you can share with procurement. We'll include the monthly usage reconciliation CSV sample and a DocuSign link for a 6-month pilot addendum.

Ben Carter
Head of Finance | Redwood Inference
